                                                   ARTICLE 5
                                                  MANAGEMENT
         1. Management. The management of the Company shall be by a Manager, who shall be the only person
empowered to bind the Company. Except as specifically set forth to the contrary herein, the Manager shall have the
authority to make all decisions for the Company and all decisions of the Manager shall be binding upon the Company.
       2. Certain Powers of Manager. The Manager shall have the exclusive power and authority, on behalf of the
Company, in accordance with Section 1 above:
                (a) To approve the sale, exchange, mortgage or other disposition of all, or substantially all, of the
        Company’s assets which is to occur as part of a single transaction or plan and to sell and acquire property to and
        from any person or entity (“Person”) as part of an arm’s length transaction as such Manager may determine and
        upon commercially reasonable terms.
                 (b) Subject to the restrictions set forth in Section 4(6), to borrow for the Company from banks, other
        lending institutions, Persons, Members, or affiliates of the Manager or Members on such terms as the Manager
        deems appropriate so long as such terms are commercially reasonable, and in connection therewith, to
        hypothecate, encumber, and grant security interests in the assets of the Company to secure repayment of the
        borrowed sums. No debt shall be contracted or liability incurred by or on behalf of the Company except by the
        Manager or, to the extent permitted under the Act, by agents or employees of the Company expressly
        authorized to contract such debt or to incur such liability by the Manager;
                 (c) To purchase liability and other insurance to protect the Company’s property and business;
                 (d) To hold and own any Company real and/or personal properties in the name of the Company;
                 (e) To time open bank accounts in the name of the Company, and the Manager shall be the sole
        signatory thereon, unless the Manager determines otherwise.
                  (f) To invest any Company funds temporarily (by way of example but not limitation) in time
        deposits, short-term governmental obligations, commercial paper, or other investments;
                   (g) To execute on behalf of the Company all instruments and documents, including, without
        limitation: checks; drafts; notes and other negotiable instruments; mortgages, or deeds of trust; security
        agreements; financing statements; documents providing for the acquisition, mortgage or disposition of the
        Company’s property; assignments; bills of sale; leases; Company agreements; operating agreements of other
        entities; and any other instruments or documents necessary, in the opinion of the Manager, to the business of
        the Company;
                  (h) To employ accountants, legal counsel, managing agents, brokers, or other experts to perform
        services for the Company and to compensate them from Company funds. The fact that a Manager or a Member
        is directly or indirectly affiliated or connected with any such employed party shall not prohibit the Manager
        from employing that party so long as the terms of such employment are commercially reasonable;
                 (i) To enter into any and all other agreements on behalf of the Company, with any person for any
        purpose, in such forms as the Manager may approve;
                  (j) To act as an attorney in fact under any power of attorney given to the Company by any person or
        entity; and
                (k) To perform any capital improvements, rehabilitation or other work at the Property as determined
        by the Manager and to execute any contracts in connection with same.
                 (l) To determine whether to make any distributions and the amount thereof and to maintain reserves
        for the Company.
               (m) To do and perform all other acts as may be necessary or appropriate to the conduct of the
        Company’s business.
                 (n) Uri Kahanow is the Manager ("Manager") of this Company and is empowered by and under
        this Agreement to acquire from and sell property to any person or entity upon commercially reasonable
        terms as such Manager may determine without authorization from the other Members of this Company. It
        is acknowledged by all Members, that Mr. Kahanow is empowered by and under this Agreement to

         perform all acts as Manager on behalf of the Company including, but not limited to, the execution on behalf

         3. Reserved Powers. Unless authorized to do so by this Agreement or by the Manager of the Company,
no attorney-in-fact, employee, or other agent of the Company shall have any power or authority to bind the
Company in any way, to pledge its credit or to render it liable peculiarly for any purpose. No Member shall have

          4. Liability for Certain Acts. The Manager shall perform its duties in good faith, in a manner it reasonably
believes to be in the best interest of the Company, and with such care as an ordinarily prudent person in a like position
would use under similar circumstances. The Manager who so performs the duties of Manager shall not have any liability
by reason of being or having been a Manager of the Company. The Manager does not, in any way, guarantee the return
of the Members’ Capital Contributions or a profit for the member from the operations of the Company. The Manager

          5. Indemnity. To the fullest extent permitted by the Act, the Company shall indemnify, defend and hold
harmless each person and entity (an "Indemnified Person") who was or is made a party or is threatened to be made a

administrative, arbitrative or investigative (including, without limitation, an action by or in the right of the Company), or
any appeal in such a proceeding or any inquiry or investigation that could lead to such a proceeding, by reason of the fact
that he, or a person or entity of whom he is the personal representative, is or was an officer, Manager, Member,
employee or agent of the Company, or is or was serving as a director, member, manager, officer, partner, venturer,
proprietor, trustee, employee or agent of another limited liability company, corporation, partnership, joint venture, trust,
sole proprietorship, employee benefit plan or other enterprise, that is or was a Manager or Member or which has any
direct or indirect interest in the Company or any manager and all affiliates of such Indemnified Person and any entity,
whether or not affiliated with such Indemnified Person, that a judgment against such entity will have an adverse effect on
any Indemnified Person, from and against any liabilities, expenses (including, without limitation, attorneys' fees and
expenses and any other costs and expenses incurred in connection with defending such action, suit or proceeding),
judgments, penalties, fines and amounts paid in settlement actually and reasonably incurred by such Indemnified Person
in connection with such proceeding except that the provisions of this Section shall not be applicable to any liability
which is the result of a Bad Act. The Company shall indemnify its Manager and its agents from any claims alleging a
breach of duty to the Company or its Members unless it is determined that an act or omission was intentionally (a) in
breach of such Person’s duty of loyalty to the Company or its Members (b) not in good faith or involving a knowing
violation of law or (c) resulted in the receipt of an improper benefit by such Person.
           6. Manager Has No Exclusive Duty to Company. The Manager shall not be required to manage the
Company as its sole and exclusive function and it may have other business interests and may engage in other activities in
addition to those relating to the Company including any activities which directly compete with the Company. Neither
the Company nor any Member shall have any right, by virtue of this Agreement, to share or participate in such other
investments or activities of the Manager or to the income or proceeds derived therefrom. The Manager shall incur no
liability to the Company or to any of the Members as a result of engaging in any other business or venture. The Manager
shall have the right, on commercially reasonable terms, to hire an affiliate to perform all capital repairs, maintenance,
construction, rehabilitation and any other work at the Property or to perform such repairs, maintenance, construction,
rehabilitation or other work on its own, but shall have no obligation to do so.
           7. Fee for Services. The Manager may designate a company to be paid a fee of six (6%) percent of gross
revenues (the “Services Fee”) pursuant to a Services Agreement between the Company and its affiliate and no Manager
or affiliate shall be prevented from receiving that Services Fee because the Manager is also a Member of the Company.
The Services Fee shall be paid monthly and shall be adjusted at the end of each year.
          8. Reimbursements. The Company will reimburse the Manager or other companies, including affiliates, for
all actual and reasonable costs and expenses incurred in the course of its service to the Company hereunder including any
salary and other compensation paid to its employees who work at the property and who perform legal, financial analysis
and bookkeeping work.

         9. Resignation. The Manager may resign at any time by giving written notice to the Members of the
Company. The resignation of the Manager shall take effect upon receipt of the notice or at such later time as shall be

                                               ARTICLE 6
                                      ALLOCATIONS AND DISTRIBUTIONS
         1. Allocation of Profits. Allocations of profit shall be made as follows: (a) items of net income and gain
shall be allocated among the Members in the manner necessary to increase each Member’s Capital Account to an
amount equal to the amount of cash such Member would be entitled to receive pursuant to subsections (6) of this
Article if an amount of cash equal to the net positive Capital Account balances (after such allocation and after
hypothetically increasing such Capital Account balances by amounts of any Company Minimum Gain and Member
Minimum Gain that would be allocated to the Members if all Company assets were sold for an amount equal to the
Company indebtedness encumbering such assets) were distributed to the Members in the order and priority specified
in subsections (6) of this Article,
         2. Allocation of Losses. Items of net loss and deduction shall be allocated among the Members in the
manner necessary to reduce each Member’s Capital Account to an amount equal to the amount of cash such Member
would be entitled to receive pursuant to subsections (6) of this Article if an amount of cash equal to the net positive
Capital Account balances after such allocation and after hypothetically increasing such Capital Account balances by
amounts of any Company Minimum Gain and Member Minimum Gain that would be allocated to the Members if all
Company assets were sold for an amount equal to the Company indebtedness encumbering such assets) were distributed
to the Members in the order and priority specified in subsections (6) of this Article.
          3. Other Allocations. It is the intention of the Members that allocations of profits and losses made to the
Members have economic effect equivalence in accordance with the regulations under Internal Revenue Code Section
704(b). The provisions of Section 6(1) and Section 6(2) shall be interpreted consistent with, and subject to, the terms
set forth on Exhibit A attached hereto, which terms shall be incorporated herein as if restated in full in this Article 6,
as applicable to the operations of the Company.
         4.   Capital Accounts. Each Member shall have a Capital Account which shall consist of its
                  (a) Capital Contributions to the capital of the Company;
                  (b) Plus, the amount of profits allocated to it pursuant to Section 6(1);
                  (c) Minus, the amount of losses associated to it pursuant to this Article 6(2); and
                  (d) Minus, all amounts distributed to or on behalf of such Member pursuant hereto;
         5. Interest on Capital Accounts. No interest shall be paid or accrued on any Member’s Capital Account
except as herein provided.
          6. Distributions. All distributions of the Company shall be distributed to the Members in the following order
of priority, subject to the provision of Section 7 below:
                  a)   to the Members in accordance with and in proportion to each Member’s accrued but undistributed
                       Preferred Distribution, if agreed to by the parties;
                  b) to the Members in accordance with and in proportion to each Member’s capital contribution in
                     the Company until each Member receives the total amount of its capital contributions;
                  c)   to the Members in accordance with the Members’ Membership Interests in the Company as
                       provided in Section 3(1).

                                                   ARTICLE 7
                                              TRANSFER OF INTEREST

          1. Prohibition Against Transfer. Except as hereinafter set forth, no Member may sell, assign, transfer,
encumber or otherwise dispose of all or any part of the property of the Company or its interest in the Company whether
direct or indirect through any number of tiers without the consent of the Manager which consent may be withheld in its
sole and absolute discretion. It is the intent of this section to maintain the control of the Company in the natural persons
who own the Company on the Effective Date. Any transfer not in accordance with this Article 7 shall have no effect and
will not be recognized by the Company. Upon the death of any individual who has interest in the Company on the date
that the Company initially acquires the property, such interest shall devise to his heirs.

          2. Assignment by Members. Any Member shall have the right to transfer or assign all or part of its share to
a subsidiary or affiliated company or to an entity in which the Member is the Manager or controlling party with full
control of all aspects of the entity (hereinafter a “Permitted Assignee”). Any Member or any Permitted Assignee may
also transfer or assign part, but not all, of its or their share to individuals who control that Member or any Permitted
Assignee, to heir lineal descendants (hereinafter “Family Members”), or to any or all of the foregoing; provided,
however, transfers or assignments to Family Members shall not include any voting rights, which voting rights shall be
reserved by the Member or the Permitted Assignee which is making the transfer or assignment to the Family Member.
         3. Assumption by Assignee. Any assignee or transferee who acquires all or part of a share in the Company
pursuant to the terms of this Agreement or otherwise shall take such share subject to all of the terms and conditions of
this Agreement; and such person shall not be considered to have such share until he shall agree in writing to assume the
obligations of his assignor or transfer hereunder and if such person is not at the time of such transfer a party to this
Agreement, to otherwise be bound by the terms and conditions of this Agreement.
                                                      ARTICLE 8
                                                     DISSOLUTION
          1. Termination or Dissolution. Upon termination of the Company, the Company shall be dissolved and its
affairs and business shall be liquidated forthwith. All property of the Company shall be sold or otherwise disposed of
and the new proceeds therefor, if any, and the remaining assets of the Company shall be applied first to satisfy the costs,
expenses, charges and liabilities of the Company, either by payment or the establishment of an adequate reserve to cover
the same and the balance shall be distributed to the Members in accordance with the distribution provisions of this
Agreement.
         2. Tax Effect of Termination or Dissolution. It is the intention of the Members that allocations made to the
Members have economic effect equivalence in accordance with the regulations under Internal Revenue Code Section
704(b). The provisions of this Section 8(2) shall be interpreted consistent with, and subject to, the terms set forth on
Exhibit A attached hereto, which terms shall be incorporated herein as if restated in full in this Article 8, as
applicable to the termination and dissolution of the Company. If a Member has a deficit balance in its Capital
Account (after giving effect to all contributions, distributions, and allocations for all tax years, including the tax year
in which such liquidation occurs), such Member shall have no obligation to make any contribution to the capital of
the Company with respect to such deficit, and such deficit shall not be considered a debt owed to the Company or to
any other Person for any purpose whatsoever.
         3. Dissolution Procedure. Within thirty (30) days of the termination of the Company or an event of
Dissolution as set forth in this Agreement, the Manager shall retain the services of a qualified appraiser to value all of the
property of the Company. The assets of the Company shall be distributed to the Members if practical and if acceptable
to all Members, or sold at prices in accordance with said appraisal.
         4. Continuation. Nothing contained herein shall be construed as limiting the ability of the remaining
Members from execution of a new Agreement and continuing the business of the Company, all in accordance with the
Act and the applicable provision of the Code.
        5. Events of Dissolution. The Company shall dissolve and commence to wind up its affairs upon the
occurrence of any of the following, in addition to those set forth elsewhere herein (each a “Dissolution Event”):



                                                              7

===== PAGE 188 =====
                (a) The written consent of the manager and the members holding two-thirds (2/3) of all of the
         Membership Interests to dissolve;
                  (b) The entry of a decree of judicial dissolution under Section 18-802 of the Act; or
                   (c) Ninety (90) days after the date on which the Company no longer has at least one Member, unless
         at least one new Member is admitted to the Company within such 90-day period by such Member’s legal
         representative.
         The Members hereby agree that, notwithstanding any provision of the Act, the Company shall not dissolve
         prior to the occurrence of a Dissolution Event. For avoidance of doubt, any event that terminates the continued
         membership of any Member shall not cause the Company to be dissolved or its affairs to be wound up, and
         upon the occurrence of any such event, the Company shall be continued without dissolution.

           13. Heter Iska. The undersigned members of the Company hereby declare and admit that all advances made
between themselves with respect to capital contributions, loans to the company, capital calls, or any other mortgages,
guarantees, preferred investments, or any other advances, that would violate any of the laws of Ribbis shall be structured
as an Iska investment subject to the following terms. In exchange for the monies advanced, the recipient/beneficiary shall
transfer to the investor a share (of equal value) in his assets as an Iska. In the event that no such investment exists, or if
the recipient participates in a more lucrative investment opportunity in the future, the recipient shall assign a share of that
investment to the investor. This investment shall be owned by the investing partner, and all profits, capital gains, or
losses shall be his sole responsibility. The recipient shall have complete authority to manage this investment on behalf of
the investor, in the manner deemed most beneficial to the investor. Any investment owned by the recipient may be used
to create this Iska, provided that the venture is Halachacly permissible. This Iska may only be collected from the assets of
the Company and the investor shall have no claim against the personal assets of any of the recipients, unless otherwise
specified in an agreement between the parties. The recipient shall receive five percent of the profits as compensation for
his services managing this Iska, and shall be liable for the monies as a watchman. The recipient must verify any claim of
loss through the testimony of two Halachacly acceptable witnesses in an Orthodox Jewish court of law. Any claim
regarding the amount of profits generated by the joint venture must be verified with a solemn oath, administered by an
Orthodox Jewish court of law. In addition, the investor may demand full access to all legal records, documents, financial
statements or receipts that the investor deems necessary to verify the claims of the recipient. In the event of a claim of
loss, the investor may demand a full and immediate payment of the remaining balance of this Iska. It is agreed that if the
recipient pays the amount equal to the principal, interest, penalties, default rates, preferred returns, membership dilution,
buyout rights, or other benefits called for by this Agreement, as per the payment schedule of this Agreement, as payment
for the investor's share of the principal and profits of the Iska investment, the investor shall waive his right to demand
verification of the results of the investment. Any additional profits shall belong solely to the recipient. Such payment
shall reflect a final settlement, and the recipient shall have no further claim for compensation, management or services
fees, unless specified to the contrary in other agreements executed between the parties. Any payments made that are not
justified by this Iska agreement shall reduce the principal balance of this Iska. However, any future payments made to
avoid providing the abovementioned verification, shall be increased to compensate for any discrepancy. This section
shall override any other section, even those that do not reference this section. Any mention of loans or interest shall be
interpreted as an Iska and to payments mentioned above. This declaration is legally binding and may be enforced in any
Jewish or civil court, even in the event that one of the parties was unaware of its existence. This agreement has been
executed in an effective manner and with a proper Kinyan, if required.

         14. Counterparts. This Agreement may be executed in counterparts which together shall constitute one fully
executed Agreement. This Agreement shall become effective upon the exchange of facsimile or emailed signatures. A
copy of any parties’ signature shall be the same as an original.

                                                 Exhibit A

                                              Tax Provisions

1.   Special Allocations. The following special allocations shall be made in the following order:

              (a)       Minimum Gain Chargeback. Except as otherwise provided in Regulations Section
     1.704-2(f), notwithstanding any other provision of this Exhibit, if there is a net decrease in Company
     Minimum Gain during any fiscal year, each Member shall be specially allocated items of Company income
     and gain for such fiscal year (and, if necessary, subsequent fiscal years) in an amount equal to such
     Member's share of the net decrease in Company Minimum Gain, determined in accordance with
     Regulations Section 1.704-2(g). Allocations pursuant to the previous sentence shall be made in proportion
     to the respective amounts required to be allocated to each Member pursuant thereto. The items to be so
     allocated shall be determined in accordance with Regulations Sections 1.704-2(f)(6) and 1.704-2(j)(2). This
     Section 1(a) is intended to comply with the minimum gain chargeback requirement in Regulations Section
     1.704-2(f) and shall be interpreted consistently therewith.

              (b)       Member Minimum Gain Chargeback. Except as otherwise provided in Regulations
     Section 1.704-2(i)(4), notwithstanding any other provision of this Exhibit, if there is a net decrease in
     Member Nonrecourse Debt Minimum Gain attributable to a Member Nonrecourse Debt during any fiscal
     year, each Member who has a share of the Member Nonrecourse Debt Minimum Gain attributable to such
     Member Nonrecourse Debt, determined in accordance with Regulations Section 1.704-2(i)(5), shall be
     specially allocated items of Company income and gain for such fiscal year (and, if necessary, subsequent
     fiscal years) in an amount equal to such Member's share of the net decrease in Member Nonrecourse Debt,
     determined in accordance with Regulations Section 1.704-2(i)(4). Allocations pursuant to the previous
     sentence shall be made in proportion to the respective amounts required to be allocated to each Member
     pursuant thereto. The items to be so allocated shall be determined in accordance with Regulations Sections
     1.704-2(i)(4) and 1.704-2(j)(2). This Section 1(b) is intended to comply with the minimum gain chargeback
     requirement in Regulations Section 1.704-2(i)(4) and shall be interpreted consistently therewith.

              (c)       Qualified Income Offset. In the event any Member unexpectedly receives any
     adjustments, allocations, or distributions described in Regulations Section 1.704-1(b)(2)(ii)(d)(4), Section
     1.704-1(b)(2)(ii)(d)(5), or Section 1.704-1(b)(2)(ii)(d)(6), items of Company income and gain shall be
     specially allocated to such Member in an amount and manner sufficient to eliminate, to the extent required
     by the Regulations, the deficit balance in the Capital Account of such Member as quickly as possible,
     provided, that an allocation pursuant to this Section 1(c) shall be made only if and to the extent that such
     Member would have an deficit balance in its Capital Account after all other allocations provided for in this
     Exhibit have been tentatively made as if this Section 1(c) were not in this Exhibit.

               (d)       Gross Income Allocation. In the event any Member has a deficit Capital Account at the
     end of any fiscal year that is in excess of the amount such Member is obligated to restore pursuant to the
     penultimate sentences of Regulations Sections 1.704-2(g)(1) and 1.704-2(i)(5), such Member shall be
     specially allocated items of Company income and gain in the amount of such excess as quickly as possible,
     provided, that an allocation pursuant to this Section 1(d) shall be made only if and to the extent that such
     Member would have a deficit Capital Account in excess of such amount after all other allocations provided
     for in this Exhibit have been made as if Section 1(c) and this Section 1(d) were not in this Agreement.

              (e)        Nonrecourse Deductions. Nonrecourse Deductions for any fiscal year shall be specially
     allocated to all of the Members in proportion to the Membership Interests of the Members.

              (f)     Member Nonrecourse Deductions. Any Member Nonrecourse Deductions for any fiscal
     year shall be specially allocated to the Member who bears the economic risk of loss with respect to the
     Member Nonrecourse Debt to which such Member Nonrecourse Deductions are attributable in accordance
     with Regulations Section 1.704-2(i)(1).



                                                     11

===== PAGE 192 =====
                   (g)      Section 754 Adjustments. To the extent an adjustment to the adjusted tax basis of any
         Company asset pursuant to Code Section 734(b) or Section 743(b) is required, pursuant to Regulations
         Section 1.704-1(b)(2)(iv)(m)(2) or Section 1.704-1(b)(2)(iv)(m)(4), to be taken into account in determining
         Capital Accounts as the result of a distribution to a Member in complete liquidation of such Member's
         interest in the Company, the amount of such adjustment to the Capital Accounts shall be treated as an item
         of gain (if the adjustment increases the basis of the asset) or as an item of loss (if the adjustment decreases
         such basis), and such gain or loss shall be specially allocated to the Members in accordance with their
         interests in the Company in the event Regulations Section 1.704-1(b)(2)(iv)(m)(2) applies, or to the
         Member to whom such distribution was made in the event Regulations Section 1.704-1(b)(2)(iv)(m)(4)
         applies.

         2.       Curative Allocations. The allocations set forth in Section 1 (the “Regulatory Allocations”) are
intended to comply with certain requirements of the Regulations. It is the intent of the Members that, to the extent
possible, all Regulatory Allocations shall be offset either with other Regulatory Allocations or with special
allocations of other items of Company income, gain, loss, or deduction pursuant to this Section 2. Therefore,
notwithstanding any other provision of this Exhibit (other than the Regulatory Allocations), the Manager shall make
such offsetting special allocations of Company income, gain, loss, or deduction in whatever manner it determines
appropriate so that, after such offsetting allocations are made, each Member's Capital Account balance is, to the
extent possible, equal to the Capital Account balance such Member would have had if the Regulatory Allocations
were not part of this Agreement and all Company items were allocated pursuant to Article 6(1) and Article 6(2). In
exercising their discretion under this Section 2, the Manager shall take into account future Regulatory Allocations
under Sections 1(a) and 1(b) that, although not yet made, are likely to offset other Regulatory Allocations previously
made under Sections 1(e) and 1(f).

         3.        Loss Limitation. Losses allocated pursuant to Article 6(1) hereof shall not exceed the maximum
amount of losses that can be allocated without causing any Member to have an deficit balance in its Capital Account
at the end of any fiscal year. In the event some but not all of the Members would have a deficit balance in its Capital
Account as a consequence of an allocation of losses pursuant to Article 6(1) hereof, the limitation set forth in this
Section 3 shall be applied on a Member by Member basis and losses not allocable to any Member as a result of such
limitation shall be allocated to the other Members in accordance with the positive balances in such Members’
Capital Accounts so as to allocate the maximum permissible losses to each Member under Regulations Section
1.704-1(b)(2)(ii)(d).

         4.       Other Allocation Rules.

         (a)     For purposes of determining the profits, losses, or any other items allocable to any period, profits,
losses, and any such other items shall be determined on a daily, monthly, or other basis, as determined by the
Manager using any permissible method under Code Section 706 and the Regulations thereunder.

           (b)     Solely for purposes of determining a Member's proportionate share of the "excess nonrecourse
liabilities" of the Company within the meaning of Regulations Section 1.752-3(a)(3), the Members' interests in
Company profits are in proportion to the Membership Interests of such Members.

         (c)     In the event that the Company has taxable income that is characterized as ordinary income under
the recapture provisions of the Code, each Member's distributive share of taxable gain or loss from the sale of
Company assets shall (to the extent possible) include a proportionate share of this recapture income equal to such
Member's share of prior cumulative depreciation deductions with respect to the assets that gave rise to the recapture
income.

          (d)      It is the intention of the parties that the Capital Accounts of the Members immediately before the
liquidation of the Company shall be as nearly equal as possible to the amounts that they would receive in such
liquidation if Article 6(8) governed liquidating distributions. Therefore, in the fiscal year the Company is liquidated,
should there be any difference between the Capital Accounts of the Members and the amounts they would otherwise
be entitled to receive in liquidation if Article 6(8) governed, then profits and losses in such fiscal year shall be
specially allocated among the Members so that, to the maximum extent possible, their Capital Accounts shall equal
the amounts to which they would be entitled if Article 6(8) governed liquidating distributions.

        5.       Tax Allocations: Code Section 704(c). In accordance with Code Section 704(c) and the
Regulations thereunder, income, gain, loss, and deduction with respect to any property contributed to the capital of
the Company shall, solely for tax purposes, be allocated among the Members so as to take account of any variation
between the adjusted basis of such property to the Company for federal income tax purposes and its initial Gross
Asset Value using the "traditional method" pursuant to the Regulations under Code Section 704(c).

         In the event the Gross Asset Value of any Company asset is adjusted pursuant to subparagraph (ii) of the
definition of “Gross Asset Value” set forth below, subsequent allocations of income, gain, loss, and deduction with
respect to such asset shall take account of any variation between the adjusted basis of such asset for federal income
tax purposes and its Gross Asset Value in the same manner as under Code Section 704(c) and the Regulations
thereunder.

          Any elections or other decisions relating to such allocations shall be made by the Manager in any manner
that reasonably reflects the purpose and intention of this Agreement. Allocations pursuant to this Section 5 are solely
for purposes of federal, state, and local taxes and shall not affect, or in any way be taken into account in computing,
any Member's Capital Account or share of profits, losses, other items, or distributions pursuant to any provision of
this Agreement.

For purposes of this Exhibit A, the following definitions shall apply:

         (i)      “Company Minimum Gain” has the same meaning as is given to the term “partnership minimum
gain” in Sections 1.704-2(b)(2) and 1.704-2(d) of the Regulations.

         (ii)     “Company Nonrecourse Debt” has the same meaning as is given to the term “partner nonrecourse
debt” in Section 1.704-2(b)(4) of the Regulations.

         (iii)    “Company Nonrecourse Debt Minimum Gain” means an amount, with respect to each Member
Nonrecourse Debt, equal to the Company Minimum Gain that would result if such Member Nonrecourse Debt were
treated as a Nonrecourse Liability, determined in accordance with Section 1.704-2(i)(3) of the Regulations.

        (iv)    “Company Nonrecourse Deductions” has the same meaning as is given to the term “partner
nonrecourse deductions” in Sections 1.704-2(i)(1) and 1.704-2(i)(2) of the Regulations.

         (v)      “Gross Asset Value” means, with respect to any asset, the asset's adjusted basis for federal income
tax purposes, except as follows:

                  (i) The initial Gross Asset Value of any asset contributed by a Member to the Company shall be
         the gross fair market value of such asset, as determined by the contributing Member and the Manager.

                  (ii) The Gross Asset Values of all Company assets shall be adjusted to equal their respective gross
         fair market values, as determined by the Manager, as of the following times: (a) the acquisition of an
         additional interest in the Company by any new or existing Member in exchange for more than a de minimis
         Capital Contribution; (b) the distribution by the Company to any Member of more than a de minimis
         amount of property as consideration for an interest in the Company; and (c) the liquidation of the Company
         within the meaning of Regulations Section 1.704-1(b)(2)(ii)(g); provided, however, that adjustments
         pursuant to clauses (a) and (b) above shall be made only if the Manager reasonably determines that such
         adjustments are necessary or appropriate to reflect the relative economic interests of the Members in the
         Company.

                  (iii) The Gross Asset Value of any Company asset distributed to any Member shall be adjusted to
         equal the gross fair market value of such asset on the date of distribution as determined by the distributee
         and the Manager.

                  (iv)      The Gross Asset Values of Company assets shall be increased (or decreased) to reflect
         any adjustments to the adjusted basis of such assets pursuant to Code Section 734(b) or Section 743(b), but
         only to the extent that such adjustments are taken into account in determining Capital Accounts pursuant to
         Regulations Section 1.704-1(b)(2)(iv)(m) and subparagraph (vi) of the definition of “Profits” and “Losses”

TRYKO DELTA HOLDINGS, LLC ("Tryko") and NORMAN ROKEACH, an individual ("Rokeach").

Agreement to control the operations ofQuinto Delta LLC, a limited liability company fonned under and pursuant to

the tenns, provisions and conditions hereinafter set forth. This Agreement supersedes and replaces in its entirety

                                                ARTICLE4
                                          CAPITAL CONTRIBUTIONS
         I. Initial Capital Contributions. All Capital Contributions of the Company shall be contributed in
accordance with the Membership Interests of the Members, provided that Rokeach shall not be obligated to make
any Capital Contributions unless Rokeach has such obligation pursuant to the Quinto Agreement. The Manager
does not, in any way, guarantee the return of the Members' Capital Contributions or a profit for the Members from
the operations of the Company. In addition to the Capital Contributions of the Members, upon acquisition of the
Company's property, the Company may borrow additional funds from all of the Members or an affiliate of the
Company which loan shall be evidenced by a note and shall be repaid as set forth therein.

         2. Estimated Expenses. The Manager shall, from time to time, but not more often than quarterly,
estimate the cash requirements of the Company for an ensuing period of time and the Members shall each be
responsible to pay their pro rata share of such estimated cash requirements in accordance with the Members'
Membership Interests.
         3. Members Failure to Make Contributions. Upon demand by the Manager, each Member agrees to
pay, within ten (10) days after receiving a demand therefore, its pro rata share (based upon such Member's interest
in the Company pursuant to Section 3(1) and irrespective of the percentage of the Initial Capital Contributions of
each Member) of all costs, expenses or charges with respect to the ownership, construction, operation, maintenance
and upkeep of the Company's property to the extent that all of said costs, expenses or charges cannot be paid out of
the cash flow (as herein defined) if any, of the Company, provided, however, that Rokeach's obligation to make the
Capital Call is subject to the provisions of the Quinto Agreement. The provisions of this paragraph shall be binding
upon the Members and the Company, but such provisions shall not inure to the benefit of any other person including
any creditors of the Company. Any distribution due to a Member who has defaulted in payment of any required
Capital Contribution shall be first applied to any reimbursement owed by that defaulting Member to the Company
plus interest at the rate agreed to by the parties, which shall compound monthly, pursuant to the heter iska in Section
9(12) below (the "Heter lska"), or to another Member who has made the Capital Contributions on the part of the
defaulting Member plus interest as provided for in Section 5 of this Article, before distribution of the remainder, if
any, to the defaulting Member.
          4. Option to Assist Defaulting Member. If any Member shall default in the payment of any sums
required to be paid by it to the Company hereunder (the "Defaulting Member"), the Manager shall notify the other
Members regarding such default and the other Members may (the "Assisting Member"), without the Company
waiving any claims for breach, cure such default for the account of the Defaulting Member (the "Default Loan").
The Defaulting Member shall be responsible to repay (solely out of any distribution to which the defaulting Member
may be entitled) the Default Loan with interest at the rate agreed to by the parties which shall compound monthly
and shall be subject to the Heter !ska. Until the Default Loan is repaid in full with interest as herein provided, all
distributions which would otherwise have been made to the Defaulting Member shall be paid to the Assisting
Member, to be applied first to accrued interest and then to principal. Any distribution to the Assisting Member in
connection with the Default Loan pursuant to this Paragraph (or to the Company pursuant to Section 4 of this Article)
shall be considered a distribution to the Defaulting Member. In the event more than one Member wishes to make

                                                ARTICLE7
                                           TRANSFER OF INTEREST

          I. Prohibition Against Transfer. Except as hereinafter set forth, no Member may sell, assign, transfer,
encumber or otherwise dispose of all or any part of the property of the Company or its interest in the Company
whether direct or indirect through any number of tiers without the consent of the Manager which consent may be
withheld in its sole and absolute discretion. It is the intent of this section to maintain the control of the Company in
the natural persons who own the Company on the Effective Date. Any transfer not in accordance with this Article
7 shall have no effect and will not be recognized by the Company. Upon the death of any individual who has interest
in the Company on the date that the Company initially acquires the property, such interest shall devise to his heirs.

          2. Assignment by Members. Any Member shall have the right to transfer or assign all or part of its share
to a subsidiary or affiliated company or to an entity in which the Member is the Manager or controlling party with
full control of all aspects of the entity (hereinafter a "Permitted Assignee"). Any Member or any Permitted Assignee
may also transfer or assign part, but not all, of its or their share to individuals who control that Member or any
Permitted Assignee, to heir lineal descendants (hereinafter "Family Members"), or to any or all of the foregoing;
provided, however, transfers or assignments to Family Members shall not include any voting rights, which voting
rights shall be reserved by the Member or the Permitted Assignee which is making the transfer or assignment to the
Family Member.
          3. Assumption by Assignee. Any assignee or transferee who acquires all or part of a share in the
Company pursuant to the terms of this Agreement or otherwise shall take such share subject to all of the tenns and
conditions of this Agreement; and such person shall not be considered to have such share until he shall agree in
writing to assume the obligations of his assignor or transfer hereunder and if such person is not at the time of such
transfer a party to this Agreement, to otherwise be bound by the terms and conditions of this Agreement.
          4. No Right to Force Assignment. Neither party shall have the right to force the other party to sell its
interests to the other in any court or other proceeding.

           I. Termination or Dissolution. Upon termination of the Company, the Company shall be dissolved and

reserve to cover the same and the balance shall be distributed to the Members in accordance with the distribution
provisions of this Agreement.
         2. Tax Effect of Termination or Dissolution. It is the intention of the Members that allocations made
to the Members have economic effect equivalence in accordance with the regulations under Internal Revenue Code
Section 704(b). The provisions of this Section 8(2) shall be interpreted consistent with, and subject to, the terms
set forth on Exhibit A attached hereto, which terms shall be incorporated herein as if restated in full in this
Article 8, as applicable to the termination and dissolution of the Company. If a Member has a deficit balance in
its Capital Account (after giving effect to all contributions, distributions, and allocations for all tax years,
including the tax year in which such liquidation occurs), such Member shall have no obligation to make any
contribution to the capital of the Company with respect to such deficit, and such deficit shall not be considered
a debt owed to the Company or to any other Person for any purpose whatsoever.
         3. Dissolution Procedure. Within thirty (30) days of the termination of the Company or an event of
Dissolution as set forth in this Agreement, the Manager shall retain the services of a qualified appraiser to value all

                                            Tax Provisions

I.   Special Allocations. The following special allocations shall be made in the following order:

              (a)      Minimum Gain Chargeback. Except as otherwise provided in Regulations Section
     1.704-2(f), notwithstanding any other provision of this Exhibit, if there is a net decrease in Company
     Minimum Gain during any fiscal year, each Member shall be specially allocated items of Company
     income and gain for such fiscal year (and, if necessary, subsequent fiscal years) in an amount equal to
     such Member's share of the net decrease in Company Minimum Gain, determined in accordance with
     Regulations Section I.704-2(g). Allocations pursuant to the previous sentence shall be made in
     proportion to the respective amounts required to be allocated to each Member pursuant thereto. The
     items to be so allocated shall be determined in accordance with Regulations Sections 1.704-2(f)(6) and
     1.704-2(j)(2). This Section l (a) is intended to comply with the minimum gain chargeback requirement
     in Regulations Section l .704-2(f) and shall be interpreted consistently therewith.

              (b)      Member Minimum Gain Chargeback. Except as otherwise provided in Regulations
     Section 1.704-2(i)(4), notwithstanding any other provision of this Exhibit, if there is a net decrease in
     Member Nonrecourse Debt Minimum Gain attributable to a Member Nonrecourse Debt during any
     fiscal year, each Member who has a share of the Member Nonrecourse Debt Minimum Gain attributable
     to such Member Nonrecourse Debt, determined in accordance with Regulations Section l .704-2(i)(5),
     shall be specially allocated items of Company income and gain for such fiscal year (and, if necessary,
     subsequent fiscal years) in an amount equal to such Member's share of the net decrease in Member
     Nonrecourse Debt, determined in accordance with Regulations Section 1.704-2(i)(4). Allocations
     pursuant to the previous sentence shall be made in proportion to the respective amounts required to be
     allocated to each Member pursuant thereto. The items to be so allocated shall be determined in
     accordance with Regulations Sections I.704-2(i)(4) and l .704-2(j)(2). This Section 1 (b) is intended to
     comply with the minimum gain chargeback requirement in Regulations Section 1.704-2(i)(4) and shall
     be interpreted consistently therewith.

              (c)      Qualified Income Offset. In the event any Member unexpectedly receives any
     adjustments, allocations, or distributions described in Regulations Section l .704-l (b)(2)(ii)(d)(4),
     Section I. 704-1(b )(2)(ii)(d)(5), or Section 1.704-1(b)(2)(ii)(d)(6), items of Company income and gain
     shall be specially allocated to such Member in an amount and manner sufficient to eliminate, to the
     extent required by the Regulations, the deficit balance in the Capital Account of such Member as quickly
     as possible, provided, that an allocation pursuant to this Section 1 (c) shall be made only if and to the
     extent that such Member would have an deficit balance in its Capital Account after all other allocations
     provided for in this Exhibit have been tentatively made as if this Section 1(c) were not in this Exhibit.

              (d)      Gross Income Allocation. In the event any Member has a deficit Capital Account at
     the end of any fiscal year that is in excess of the amount such Member is obligated to restore pursuant
     to the penultimate sentences of Regulations Sections l .704-2(g)(l ) and l .704-2(i)(5), such Member
     shall be specially allocated items of Company income and gain in the amount of such excess as quickly
     as possible, provided, that an allocation pursuant to this Section 1(d) shall be made only if and to the
     extent that such Member would have a deficit Capital Account in excess of such amount after all other
     allocations provided for in this Exhibit have been made as if Section 1(c) and this Section 1(d) were not
     in this Agreement.

              (e)      Nonrecourse Deductions. Nonrecourse Deductions for any fiscal year shall be
     specially allocated to all of the Members in proportion to the Membership Interests of the Members.

              (f)       Member Nonrecourse Deductions. Any Member Nonrecourse Deductions for any
     fiscal year shall be specially allocated to the Member who bears the economic risk of loss with respect

        to the Member Nonrecourse Debt to which such Member Nonrecourse Deductions are attributable in
        accordance with Regulations Section l .704-2(i)(l) .

                 (g)      Section 754 Adjustments. To the extent an adjustment to the adjusted tax basis ofany
        Company asset pursuant to Code Section 73 4(b) or Section 74 3(b) is required, pursuant to Regulations
        Section 1.704-1(b)(2)(iv)(m)(2) or Section I.704-1(b)(2)(iv)(m)(4), to be taken into account in
        determining Capital Accounts as the result ofa distribution to a Member in complete liquidation ofsuch
        Member's interest in the Company, the amount of such adjustment to the Capital Accounts shall be
        treated as an item of gain (if the adjustment increases the basis of the asset) or as an item of loss (if the

        applies, or to the Member to whom such distribution was made in the event Regulations Section
        I. 704-1(b)(2)(iv)(m)(4) applies.

         2.       Curative Allocations. The allocations set forth in Section 1 (the "Regulatory Allocations")
are intended to comply with certain requirements of the Regulations. It is the intent of the Members that, to the
extent possible, all Regulatory Allocations shall be offset either with other Regulatory Allocations or with special
allocations of other items of Company income, gain, loss, or deduction pursuant to this Section 2. Therefore,
notwithstanding any other provision of this Exhibit (other than the Regulatory Allocations) , the Manager shall
make such offsetting special allocations of Company income, gain, loss, or deduction in whatever manner it
determines appropriate so that, after such offsetting allocations are made, each Member's Capital Account
balance is, to the extent possible, equal to the Capital Account balance such Member would have had if the
Regulatory Allocations were not part of this Agreement and all Company items were allocated pursuant to
Article 6(1) and Article 6(2) . In exercising their discretion under this Section 2, the Manager shall take into
account future Regulatory Allocations under Sections I(a) and 1(b) that, although not yet made, are likely to
offset other Regulatory Allocations previously made under Sections l(e) and l(t).

         3.        Loss Limitation. Losses allocated pursuant to Article 6(1) hereof shall not exceed the
maximum amount of losses that can be allocated without causing any Member to have an deficit balance in its
Capital Account at the end of any fiscal year. In the event some but not all of the Members would have a deficit
balance in its Capital Account as a consequence of an allocation of losses pursuant to Article 6( I) hereof, the
limitation set forth in this Section 3 shall be applied on a Member by Member basis and losses not allocable to
any Member as a result ofsuch limitation shall be allocated to the other Members in accordance with the positive
balances in such Members' Capital Accounts so as to allocate the maximum permissible losses to each Member
under Regulations Section 1.704-l(b)(2)(ii)(d) .

         4.       Other Allocation Rules.

          (a)      For purposes of determining the profits, losses, or any other items allocable to any period,
profits, losses, and any such other items shall be determined on a daily, monthly, or other basis, as determined
by the Manager using any permissible method under Code Section 706 and the Regulations thereunder.

          (b)       Solely for purposes ofdetermining a Member's proportionate share of the "excess nonrecourse
liabilities" of the Company within the meaning of Regulations Section J.752-3(a)(3 ) , the Members' interests in
Company profits are in proportion to the Membership Interests of such Members.

        (c)      In the event that the Company has taxable income that is characterized as ordinary income
under the recapture provisions of the Code, each Member's distributive share of taxable gain or loss from the
sale ofCompany assets shall (to the extent possible) include a proportionate share ofthis recapture income equal
to such Member's share of prior cumulative depreciation deductions with respect to the assets that gave rise to
the recapture income.

         (d)      It is the intention of the parties that the Capital Accounts of the Members immediately before
the liquidation of the Company shall be as nearly equal as possible to the amounts that they would receive in
such liquidation if Article 6(8) governed liquidating distributions. Therefore, in the fiscal year the Company is


                                                         14

===== PAGE 210 =====
liquidated, should there be any difference between the Capital Accounts of the Members and the amounts they
would otherwise be entitled to receive in liquidation if Article 6(8) governed, then profits and losses in such
fiscal year shall be specially allocated among the Members so that, to the maximum extent possible, their Capital
Accounts shall equal the amounts to which they would be entitled if Article 6(8) governed liquidating
distributions.

         5.       Tax Allocations: Code Section 704(c). In accordance with Code Section 704(c) and the
Regulations thereunder, income, gain, loss, and deduction with respect to any property contributed to the capital
of the Company shall, solely for tax purposes, be allocated among the Members so as to take account of any
variation between the adjusted basis of such property to the Company for federal income tax purposes and its
initial Gross Asset Value using the "traditional method" pursuant to the Regulations under Code Section 704(c).

         In the event the Gross Asset Value of any Company asset is adjusted pursuant to subparagraph (ii) of
the definition of"Gross Asset Value" set forth below, subsequent allocations of income, gain, loss, and deduction
with respect to such asset shall take account of any variation between the adjusted basis of such asset for federal
income tax purposes and its Gross Asset Value in the same manner as under Code Section 704(c) and the
Regulations thereunder.

         Any elections or other decisions relating to such allocations shall be made by the Manager in any
manner that reasonably reflects the purpose and intention of this Agreement. Allocations pursuant to this Section
5 are solely for purposes of federal, state, and local taxes and shall not affect, or in any way be taken into account
in computing, any Member's Capital Account or share of profits, losses, other items, or distributions pursuant to
any provision of this Agreement.

For purposes of this Exhibit A, the following definitions shall apply:

      (i)      "Company Minimum Gain" has the same meaning as is given to the term "partnership
minimum gain" in Sections 1.704-2(b)(2) and 1.704-2(d) of the Regulations.

       (ii)     "Company Nonrecourse Debt" has the same meaning as is given to the term "partner
nonrecourse debt" in Section 1.704-2(b)(4) of the Regulations.

        (iii)    "Company Nonrecourse Debt Minimum Gain" means an amount, with respect to each Member
Nonrecourse Debt, equal to the Company Minimum Gain that would result if such Member Nonrecourse Debt
were treated as a Nonrecourse Liability, determined in accordance with Section I.704-2(i)(3) of the Regulations.

       (iv)    "Company Nonrecourse Deductions" has the same meaning as is given to the term "partner
nonrecourse deductions" in Sections 1.704-2(i)( I) and l.704-2(i)(2) of the Regulations.

        (v)    "Gross Asset Value" means, with respect to any asset, the asset's adjusted basis for federal
income tax purposes, except as follows:

                  (i) The initial Gross Asset Value of any asset contributed by a Member to the Company shall
         be the gross fair market value of such asset, as determined by the contributing Member and the Manager.

                  (ii) The Gross Asset Values of all Company assets shall be adjusted to equal their respective
         gross fair market values, as determined by the Manager, as of the following times: (a) the acquisition
         of an additional interest in the Company by any new or existing Member in exchange for more than a
         de minimis Capital Contribution; (b) the distribution by the Company to any Member of more than a de
         minimis amount of property as consideration for an interest in the Company; and (c) the liquidation of
         the Company within the meaning of Regulations Section 1.704-l(b)(2)(ii)(g); provided, however, that
         adjustments pursuant to clauses (a) and (b) above shall be made only if the Manager reasonably
         determines that such adjustments are necessary or appropriate to reflect the relative economic interests
         of the Members in the Company.

===== PAGE 211 =====
                  (iii) The Gross Asset Value of any Company asset distributed to any Member shall be adjusted
         to equal the gross fair market value of such asset on the date of distribution as determined by the
         distributee and the Manager.

                  (iv)     The Gross Asset Values of Company assets shall be increased (or decreased) to reflect
         any adjustments to the adjusted basis of such assets pursuant to Code Section 7 34(b) or Section 743(b),
         but only to the extent that such adjustments are taken into account in determining Capital Accounts
         pursuant to Regulations Section 1.704-1 (b)(2 )(iv)(m) and subparagraph (vi) of the definition of"Profits"
         and "Losses" set forth in this definition of "Gross Asset Value", or pursuant to Section l(e) hereof;
         provided, however, that Gross Asset Values shall not be adjusted pursuant to this subparagraph (iv) to
         the extent that an adjustment pursuant to subparagraph (ii) of this definition is required in connection
         with a transaction that would otherwise result in an adjustment pursuant to this subparagraph (iv).

or subparagraph (iv) of this definition, such Gross Asset Value shall thereafter be adjusted by the depreciation taken
into account with respect to such asset for purposes of computing profits and losses.

        (vi)      "Nonrecourse Deductions" has the meaning set forth in Section l.704-2(b)(I) of the
Regulations.

        (vii)     "Nonrecourse Liability" has the meaning set forth in Section l .704-2(b)(3) of the Regulations.

           2. Capital Accounts. Each Member shall have a Capital Account which shall consist of its
                   (a) Capital Contributions to the capital of the Company;
                   (b) Plus, the amount of profits allocated to it pursuant to Section 8( l );
                    (c) Plus, the amount of any additional cash or the fair market value of any additional property
           contributed to the capital of the Company by such Member;
                   (d) Minus, the amount of losses associated to it pursuant to Section 8( I);
                   (e) Minus, all amounts paid or distributed to such Member pursuant hereto;
                   (t) Minus, taxes; and
                   (g) Minus, depreciation.
         3. Interest on Capital Accounts. No interest shall be paid or accrued on any Member's Capital Account
except as herein provided.
         4. Distributions. The cash flow of the Company shall be distributed to the Members in accordance with
each Member's interest in the Company as provided in Section 5(1). Prior to any distribution of cash flow arising from
the sale or disposition of the majority of the Company's property, the Company shall apply such cash flow to the
payment of any unpaid expenses, outstanding loans, and the payment of the Capital Accounts of the Members, with any
remaining funds being disbursed to the Members in the same percentages as the membership interests which are held by
the Members.

                                                        ARTICLE 9
                                               TRANSFER OF (NTEREST
         I. Prohibition Against Transfer. Except as hereinafter set forth, no Member may sell, assign, transfer,
 encumber or otherwise dispose of all or any part of the property of the Company or its interest in the Company.
          2. Permitted Sales. In the event that at any time after the dare hereof a Member desires to sell, convey, or
encumber ("Transfer'') alt or part of that Member's interest in the Company, such Member may Transfer said interest to
a third party only after offering same for sale to the Members to remain ("Remaining Members") at the same price to be
paid by such third party. Notification of any proposed sale must be made to each Remaining Member in writing at least
three business days prior to any sale to a third party. If more than one Remaining Member makes a bona fide offer to
purchase such Membership Interest within said three day period, the sale shall be made to the Remaining Member who
made the highest offer payable in immediately available funds. Any sale to the Remaining Members as aforesaid must
be consummated within thirty (30) days after the sending of the written notice. If the Membership Interests are not
purchased by the Remaining Members as aforesaid, the Transfer to a third party may occur only upon the unanimous
consent of the Remaining Members, and only so long as any new Member shall agree, in writing, to all of the terms and
conditions of this Agreement. In the event such Transfer is not approved by the Remaining Members, unless the
Member desiring to transfer the interest shall notify the Company in writing to the contrary, the notice by said Member
of the intent to transfer shall be deemed to be a withdrawal and the dissolution procedure commenced.
          3. Assignment by Members. Any Member shall have the right to transfer or assign all or part of its share to
a subsidiary or affiliated company or to an entity in which Member is general partner or controlling party (hereinafter a
"Pennitted Assignee"). Any Member or any Permitted Assignee may also transfer or assign part, but not all, of its or
their share to individuals who control that Member or any Permitted Assignee, to heir lineal descendants (hereinafter
"Family Members"), or to any or all of the foregoing; provided, however, transfers or assignments to Family Members
shall not include any voting rights, which voting rights shall be reserved by the Member or the Permitted Assignee which
is making the transfer or assignment to the Family Member.
         4. Assumption by Assignee. Any assignee or transferee who acquires all or part of a share in the Company
pursuant to the terms of this Agreement or otherwise shall take such share subject to all of the tenns and conditions of
this Agreement; and such person shall not be considered to have such share until be shall agree in writing to assume the
obligations of his assignor or transfer hereunder and if such person is not at the time of such transfer a party to this
Agreement, to otherwise be bound by the tenns and conditions of this Agreement.
       5. Withdrawal. Any Member may voluntarily withdraw from the Company by written notice to the other
Members, which event shall commence the dissolution procedure herein set forth.
                                                      ARTICLE 10

          I. Termination or Dissolution. Upon tennination of the Company, the Company shall be dissolved and its
affairs and business shall be liquidated forthwith. All property of the Company shall be sold or otherwise disposed of
and the new proceeds therefor, if any, and the remaining asse1s of the Company shall be applied first to satisfy the costs,
expenses, charges and liabilities of the Company, either by payment or the establishment of an adequate reserve to cover
the same and the balance shall be distributed to the Members.
          2. Tax Effect of Termination or Dissolution. It is the intention of the Members that allocations made to the
Members have economic effect equivalence in accordance with the regulations under Internal Revenue Code Section
7004(b). If such allocations shall be deemed not to have economic effect equivalence as aforesaid, then, notwithstanding
anything herein to the contrary, (!) distribution of property upon liquidation of the Company sha!I be made in
accordance with the Member's Capital Accounts, and (2) any Member with a negative balance in its Capital Account
after distribution of all property upon liquidation of the Company shall be obligated to contribute to the Company an
amount of cash equal to such negative balance to be distributed to Members with positive balances in their Capital
Accounts.
         3. Dissolution Procedure. Within thirty (30) days of an event of Dissolution as set forth in this Operating
Agreement, or of notice of intent to withdraw, the Manager shall retain the services of a qualified appraiser to value all of
the property of the Company. The assets of the _Company shall be distributed to the Members if practical and if
acceptable to all Members, or sold at prices in accordance with said appraisal.

                                            OPERATING AGREEMENT
                                                     OF
                                         LINCOLNWOOD PROPERTY LLC

         THIS OPERATING AGREEMENT (the “Agreement”) is made and entered into as of May 15, 2020 by
QUINTO DELTA LLC (“Quinto”), UKR CONSULTING LLC and SKILLED VENTURE LLC (“Venture”)
(individually “Member” and collectively “Members”).
         In consideration of the mutual covenants herein contained, the Members hereby enter into this Operating
Agreement to control the operations of Lincolnwood Property LLC, a limited liability company formed under and
pursuant to the laws of the State of Rhode Island (hereinafter sometimes referred to as the “Company”) for the purposes
and upon the terms, provisions and conditions hereinafter set forth.
         Unless the context shall clearly indicate otherwise, all words and phrases used in this Operating Agreement
shall have the meaning set forth in the Rhode Island Limited Liability Company Act, (the “Act”).
                                                      ARTICLE 1
                                                     FORMATION
         1.   Name. The name of the Company shall be Lincolnwood Property LLC.
        2. Place of Business. The principal place of business of the Company shall be 1608 Route 88, Suite 200,
Brick, New Jersey or such other place or places as the Manager may from time to time designate.
          3. Formation; Ratification. The Company was formed by the filing of the Certificate of Formation on May
15, 2020. The Members do hereby ratify and authorize any and all actions taken in the name of the Company since the
date of formation and acknowledge that this Agreement shall control the operations of the Company from the date of its
formation.
          4. Member’s Authority. Except as otherwise expressly and specifically provided for in this Agreement or in
the Certificate of Formation, no Member shall have any authority to act for, or assume any obligations or responsibility
on behalf of, the Company or any other Member of the Company.
        5. Member’s Prior Obligations. No Member shall be responsible or liable for any obligation or debt of any
other Member incurred before the formation of the Company except as may be set forth herein, and each party
indemnifies and agrees to hold all others harmless from such obligations and indebtedness.
        6. Other Business. Nothing herein shall restrict any Member from conducting any other business or activity
whatsoever (including any operation or business or activity which competes with the business of the Company).
        7. Registered Agent. The registered agent for the Company shall be Registered Agents Inc, with an address
of 47 Wood Avenue, Suite 2, Barrington, RI 02806.
         8. Term. The Company shall continue until the earliest to occur of the sale or other disposition of all or
substantially all of the property of the Company, the incompetence or permanent disability of the sole remaining
Member or upon the approval of the Manager and three-quarters (3/4) of all of the Membership Interests, at least
coextensive with the remaining term of the Mortgage.
          9. Purposes of the Company. The purpose of the Company shall be to engage in any business in which a
limited liability company may lawfully engage in the State of Rhode Island.
          10. Powers of the Company. The Company shall at any time and from time to time have the power and
authority to do or cause to be done all things necessary or desirable to carry out the purposes of the Company described
in Section 1(9) hereof, including, but not limited to acquiring or disposing of real or personal (or mixed) property or any
interest therein and manage property for others, obtaining financing for the Company, including refinancing and further
including interim and permanent financing (and refinancing) for the acquisition and development of real property and
financing the operations of the Company, sell or transfer or mortgage or place (or suffer to be placed) an encumbrance
on any property of the Company, enter into leases or other similar arrangements, construct, reconstruct, alter, maintain,
repair and demolish improvements on or to any real property of the Company, enter into contracts with others to perform
or carry out any or all of the foregoing and to do all other things necessary or desirable to conduct the business of the
Company and to carry out the terms and conditions of this Agreement.

                                                    ARTICLE 4
                                              CAPITAL CONTRIBUTIONS
          1. Initial Capital Contributions. All Capital Contributions of the Company shall be contributed in
accordance with the Membership Interests of the Members. The Manager does not, in any way, guarantee the return of
the Members’ Capital Contributions or a profit for the Members from the operations of the Company. In addition to the
Capital Contributions of the Members, upon acquisition of the Company’s property, the Company may borrow
additional funds from all of the Members or an affiliate of the Company which loan shall be evidenced by a note and
shall be repaid as set forth therein.

          2. Estimated Expenses. The Manager shall, from time to time, but not more often than quarterly, estimate
the cash requirements of the Company for an ensuing period of time and the Members shall each be responsible to pay
their pro rata share of such estimated cash requirements in accordance with the Members’ Membership Interests.
          3. Members Failure to Make Contributions. Upon demand by the Manager, each Member agrees to pay,
within ten (10) days after receiving a demand therefore, its pro rata share (based upon such Member’s interest in the
Company pursuant to Section 3(1) and irrespective of the percentage of the Initial Capital Contributions of each
Member) of all costs, expenses or charges with respect to the ownership, construction, operation, maintenance and
upkeep of the Company’s property to the extent that all of said costs, expenses or charges cannot be paid out of the cash
flow (as herein defined) if any, of the Company. The provisions of this paragraph shall be binding upon the Members
and the Company, but such provisions shall not inure to the benefit of any other person including any creditors of the
Company. Any distribution due to a Member who has defaulted in payment of any required Capital Contribution shall
be first applied to any reimbursement owed by that defaulting Member to the Company plus interest at the rate of
eighteen (18%) percent or the highest amount allowed by law whichever is less, which shall compound monthly,
pursuant to the heter iska in Section 9(12) below (the “Heter Iska”), or to another Member who has made the Capital
Contributions on the part of the defaulting Member plus interest as provided for in Section 5 of this Article, before
distribution of the remainder, if any, to the defaulting Member.
         4. Option to Assist Defaulting Member. If any Member shall default in the payment of any sums required
to be paid by it to the Company hereunder (the “Defaulting Member”), the Manager shall notify the other Members
regarding such default and the other Members may (the “Assisting Member”), without the Company waiving any
claims for breach, cure such default for the account of the Defaulting Member (the “Default Loan”). The Defaulting
Member shall be responsible to repay (solely out of any distribution to which the defaulting Member may be entitled) the



                                                               3

===== PAGE 229 =====
Default Loan with interest at the lesser of eighteen (18%) percent or the highest amount allowed by law which shall
compound monthly and shall be subject to the Heter Iska. Until the Default Loan is repaid in full, with interest as herein
provided, all distributions which would otherwise have been made to the Defaulting Member shall be paid to the
Assisting Member, to be applied first to accrued interest and then to principal. Any distribution to the Assisting Member
in connection with the Default Loan pursuant to this Paragraph (or to the Company pursuant to Section 4 of this Article)
shall be considered a distribution to the Defaulting Member. In the event more than one Member wishes to make the
Default Loan, such Members shall each make a loan to the Defaulting Member pro rata based on the percentage interest
each such Assisting Member has to the combined Membership Interests of all Assisting Members. All amounts
contributed by the Assisting Members pursuant to this Section shall be paid within ten (10) days of the delivery by the
Manager of the notice of default.
          5. Priority of Capital Contributions. Except as may be expressly provided in this Agreement, no Member
shall have priority over any other Member, either for the return of Capital Contributions or for net profits, net losses, or
distributions; provided that this Section shall not apply to loans (as distinguished from Capital Contributions) which a
Member has made to the Company.
          6. Loans. The Manager shall have the right to borrow funds on behalf of the Company at the best available
terms, including from any Member, at any time that the Company needs funds for the continued operations thereof for a
period of ninety (90) days or less. Any loan from a Member shall accrue interest from the Company at the then
Applicable Federal Rate announced by the Internal Revenue Service plus eight (8%) percent per annum (but in no event
more than 18%) pursuant to the Heter Iska and any payments on such loan shall be first used to pay interest and then to
principal.

                   (h) To employ accountants, legal counsel, managing agents, brokers, or other experts to perform
